sections.h2: Where is Minot, North Dakota, and what are its main areas?
sections.html:
Minot is a north-central North Dakota city in Ward County, on the Drift Prairie about 110 miles north of Bismarck. The Mouse River, also called the Souris River, runs through it from west to east and splits the city roughly in half.

Locals describe three areas. North Hill is the plateau north of the river valley, the Mouse River Valley holds downtown and the older neighborhoods along the water, and South Hill is the broad area to the south. The valley sits about 160 feet below the surrounding plains, with the river at about 1,540 feet above sea level at city center. The Census Bureau estimates 47,308 residents as of July 1, 2025.

sections.h2: How did Minot get its start?
sections.html:
Minot came into existence in 1886 when the Great Northern Railway laid track through the area, and a tent town appeared almost overnight. Population passed 5,000 within five months, which earned the city its nickname, the Magic City.

The Soo Line reached Minot in 1893. In the 1950s federal money arrived with Minot Air Force Base, built in 1956 and 1957 about 13 miles north of town, and Garrison Dam on the Missouri River, finished in 1953. Later growth came from oil drilling in the Bakken Formation, which Wikipedia credits with population and infrastructure investment across the region.

For a seller, those layers mean a wide range of housing ages. Homes built over more than a century sell under the same city rules but can have very different repair needs.

sections.h2: Why does the Mouse River matter to a Minot house sale?
sections.html:
The Mouse River is the single biggest factor in how buyers and insurers look at a Minot property in or near the valley. A flood in April 1969 devastated the city, and the Army Corps of Engineers afterward straightened the river's path and built flood control structures.

The 2011 flood was larger. On June 26, 2011 the river crested at 1,561.7 feet, three feet above the previous record set in 1881. About 12,000 people were evacuated. According to Wikipedia's summary, more than 4,100 homes were affected, 2,376 of them extensively, and 805 were damaged beyond repair. North Dakota's Department of Emergency Services reported that the existing flood control system had been designed for flows of up to 5,000 cubic feet per second, and that the June 2011 flows exceeded 27,400 cubic feet per second.

  • The Mouse River Enhanced Flood Protection Project began in 2011 and is meant to reduce flood risk across the whole basin.
  • FEMA has been developing new flood insurance rate maps for the Mouse River Basin in response to the 2011 flood.
  • Project updates describe ongoing construction in downtown Minot under a phase labeled MI-6, along the east Central Avenue corridor.

If your home flooded, was repaired or was bought out in past years, keep every record. Buyers will ask about it, and the North Dakota disclosure form covers latent defects, structural systems and environmental issues. Details are on the Mouse River Flood Protection Plan site, including its flood insurance page.

sections.h2: How much does Minot Air Force Base affect the local housing market?
sections.html:
The base is the largest employer in Ward County and a major source of housing demand. The Minot Area Chamber EDC reports that the 5th Bomb Wing's economic impact analysis put the base's impact at $956.7 million in fiscal year 2025, with total on-base employment estimated at 6,957 jobs.

Counting service members, family members and civilian employees, more than 11,000 people are connected to the base. The chamber says their presence fuels demand for housing, retail, child care, schools and recreation in and around Minot.

See the chamber's summary of the base analysis.

sections.h2: What does a Minot winter do to a house?
sections.html:
Winters in Minot are long and cold, and heating, insulation and roofing are the systems a buyer's inspector checks first. The Minot Area Chamber EDC lists average winter highs of 15 degrees Fahrenheit and lows of minus 2, with average annual snowfall of 34 to 40 inches and annual precipitation of 17.24 inches.

  • Spring averages 51 degrees for highs and 31 for lows, so thaw cycles matter for roofs, gutters and basements.
  • Summers average 82 for highs and 58 for lows, and prevailing winds come from the northwest.
  • Severe weather is part of the record. A tornado destroyed the Gassman Coulee Bridge near Minot in 1898 and another passed over the city on July 22, 1920.

Wikipedia also notes that Richardson's ground squirrels are common in the inner city and can hollow out soil beneath structures. Climate figures are from the chamber's climate page.

sections.h2: How do I get around Minot, and why does that matter to buyers?
sections.html:
Three U.S. highways meet in Minot. US 2 is a four-lane divided highway running east to Grand Forks and west toward Williston, US 83 runs north to the Minot Air Force Base and south to Bismarck, and US 52 runs southeast toward Jamestown and northwest to the Canadian border at Portal.

The Minot Bypass follows alternate alignments of these roads in the northwest and northeast. Amtrak's Empire Builder stops in Minot, and Minot International Airport is served by three airlines.

sections.h2: How are property taxes billed and paid in Minot?
sections.html:
Ward County bills property tax, and the state formula applies. The State Tax Commissioner explains that assessed value is 50 percent of market value and that taxable value for a residential property is 4.5 percent of true and full value, then multiplied by the combined mill rate of every taxing entity on the parcel.

  • Real property tax is due January 1 after the year of assessment and payable without penalty until March 1.
  • A 5 percent discount applies to taxes paid in full on or before February 15, under N.D.C.C. 57-20-09.
  • For questions about your valuation, the Ward County Tax Equalization office is the starting point, and the State Tax Commissioner's Property Tax division at 701-328-3127 handles appeals.
  • Credits for primary residence, homestead and disabled veterans are listed on the state's residential property tax page.

The county posts a property tax lookup and payment portal, and its Treasurer's mailing address is PO Box 5005, Minot, ND 58702. Check the current balance before you sign a purchase agreement, because unpaid taxes and special assessments are deducted from your proceeds.

sections.h2: What permit and code rules should Minot sellers know?
sections.html:
The city's Building Safety division enforces state and local regulations on construction and alteration of structures. Minot also requires contractors in many trades to hold a city license, in addition to a State of North Dakota contractor registration, so confirm your contractor's licenses before paying for pre-sale repairs.

A city ordinance item posted on the Minot agenda center states that if the city corrects a code violation, the cost is levied as a special assessment against the property. That is why a code complaint at a house you are selling can turn into a balance that the buyer or title company will ask you to clear. The Building Safety page is at minotnd.gov.

sections.h2: What must a Minot seller disclose, and what are the selling options?
sections.html:
North Dakota law requires written disclosure of material facts in most residential sales. N.D.C.C. 47-10-02.1 applies to dwellings with up to four units, requires the seller to complete the form in good faith before the buyer signs final acceptance, and lists exceptions such as foreclosure sales and sales by a fiduciary administering an estate. Section 47-10-02.2 adds a written radon disclosure for residential property.

Minot sellers usually choose between listing with an agent, selling without one, or accepting a cash offer. A cash buyer purchases as-is, which can matter for a flood-affected house, an inherited property or a rental with tenants. Cash Home Buyers does not state prices on this page, but we can look at a Minot address and walk you through how an offer would work, with no obligation if you decline.

faqs.a: The Mouse River, also called the Souris River, runs through Minot from west to east and divides the city roughly in half. It flooded badly in 1969 and again in June 2011, and a basin-wide flood protection project that began in 2011 is still underway.

faqs.q: Is Minot Air Force Base the largest employer in the area?
faqs.a: Yes. The Minot Area Chamber EDC reports that the base is the largest employer in Ward County, with an estimated 6,957 on-base jobs and more than 11,000 people including family members and civilian employees.

faqs.q: When are Ward County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real property tax is due January 1 following the year of assessment and payable without penalty until March 1. A 5 percent discount applies if you pay in full by February 15.

faqs.q: Does flood mapping affect a Minot house sale?
faqs.a: It can come up. FEMA has been developing new flood insurance rate maps for the Mouse River Basin in response to the 2011 flood, so check the current map for your address and keep any flood-related repair records ready for buyers.

faqs.q: What happens if the city fixes a code violation on my Minot property?
faqs.a: A city ordinance item on the Minot agenda center says the cost to correct a violation can be levied as a special assessment against the property. Resolve any open complaint, or ask the Building Safety division what is outstanding, before you sell.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Minot house that was damaged in a flood?
faqs.a: Yes. You must disclose what you know about the damage, repairs and any water problems in writing under North Dakota's disclosure rules. A buyer that purchases as-is can take the house in its present condition.
